title: Extending Int
hints: Extensions can add computed properties and methods to types you don't own.
`isPrime`: trial division up to the square root. `digits`: map the characters of `String(magnitude)`. `times`: loop `self` times.
jsBridge: Extensions add methods and computed properties to existing types, even `Int`. That's like patching `Number.prototype`, but scoped by module and resolved at compile time, so it's safe and common in Swift.

compass.q: Extending `Number.prototype` is taboo in JS. Why is `extension Int` acceptable in Swift? What prevents collisions between libraries?
Can an extension override an existing method? Add a stored property?
`5.times { }` (Ruby-style) vs a plain `for _ in 0..<5`: is the extension worth it?
Which extensions are common in iOS codebases, like `Date` formatting or `View` modifiers? When do they become a dumping ground?
